verdict: Edwards' heart-valve sales grew 11% to $1.72B, led by a 44% surge in mitral and tricuspid therapies, though a $220M impairment charge held GAAP profit to $0.53 a share.

segments.name: TAVR
segments.note: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement — replacing a narrowed aortic valve through a catheter instead of open-heart surgery, led by the SAPIEN platform. Procedure growth drove the gain; prices were stable.

segments.name: TMTT
segments.note: Transcatheter mitral and tricuspid therapies (PASCAL, EVOQUE, SAPIEN M3) — repairing or replacing the heart's other valves without open surgery. Includes $3M of implantable heart-failure management revenue.

segments.name: Surgical
segments.note: Valves and tools for open-heart surgery, led by the RESILIA tissue portfolio. Includes $2M from a transitional service agreement.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company — 32.7% of sales, a touch leaner than a year ago.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the next generation of structural-heart therapies — 16.4% of sales.

opex.name: Impairment & other operating, net
opex.note: A $220M impairment of an in-process R&D asset and related fixed assets, plus $11M of restructuring and contract-termination costs, partly offset by a $13M litigation insurance recovery and $13M of other operating income.

otherDetail: Other income of $64M, net: $37M of net interest income plus $28M of other non-operating income, including a $19M unrealized gain on marketable securities. Net income in the flow is the $301M from continuing operations; $308M was attributable to Edwards shareholders after a $6M loss belonging to noncontrolling interests, matching the $0.53 diluted EPS.

takeaways.title: TAVR keeps growing
takeaways.text: TAVR sales rose 8.0% (8.8% at constant currency) on global procedure growth and modest share gains, with stable prices. Edwards raised full-year TAVR growth guidance to 9.0–9.5%.

takeaways.title: TMTT is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Mitral and tricuspid therapies surged 44% to $209M as PASCAL, EVOQUE and SAPIEN M3 adoption expanded. Full-year TMTT guidance rose to $780–$790M of sales.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS beat the GAAP story
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS of $0.80 grew 19%, while GAAP EPS of $0.53 was weighed down by the $220M impairment. Edwards raised full-year sales growth guidance to about 11.5% and adjusted EPS guidance to $2.97–$3.05.

oneTimers: A $220M impairment of an in-process research-and-development asset and fixed assets acquired in an acquisition is the main reason GAAP operating margin was 17.4% versus 30.3% adjusted.
A $13M net litigation insurance recovery this quarter compares with a $90M litigation expense a year ago — a swing that flatters the year-on-year comparison.
footerNote: Figures are GAAP, from continuing operations, rounded to the nearest $M (sales $1,715.5M in the release). Adjusted (non-GAAP) figures exclude the impairment, litigation, restructuring and similar items listed in the release reconciliation.
